t: This is the Grosvenor Hotel in Victoria, now called the Clermont, Victoria. It opened in 1862 and is Grade II* listed. It is cited as one of the first buildings in London to use a French pavilion roof, so look up at the roofline. Francis William Rowsell, a British barrister, civil servant and colonial administrator, died here in 1885. He was born in 1838, so he was only in his forties.
